residency.detail: Applies when the other spouse is a nonresident; the filing spouse must have lived in Alabama 6 months before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: A final divorce judgment cannot be entered until 30 days after the summons and complaint are filed.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irretrievable breakdown of the marriage, or complete incompatibility of temperament; fault grounds include adultery, abandonment and cruelty.

legalSeparation.detail: A court may grant a legal separation instead of a divorce.

grounds.detail: Incompatibility of temperament is the no-fault ground; joint dissolution requires incompatibility causing irremediable breakdown. Fault grounds include adultery.

propertyDivision.detail: Property acquired during marriage is divided in a just manner without regard to fault.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Support is set as a percentage of the obligor parent's adjusted income under Civil Rule 90.3.

legalSeparation.detail: Legal separation may be granted for incompatibility when staying married protects significant interests; one party must be a resident.

residency.detail: One spouse must be domiciled in Arizona (or stationed there in the military) for 90 days before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: No decree, trial or hearing until 60 days after service or acceptance of process.

grounds.detail: The marriage is irretrievably broken; covenant marriages are limited to the grounds in A.R.S. § 25-903.

propertyDivision.detail: Community and jointly held property is divided equitably, though not necessarily in kind, without regard to marital misconduct.

legalSeparation.detail: Court enters a decree of legal separation on the same findings as dissolution.

residency.detail: 60 days' residence before filing, plus 3 full months' residence before the final decree.

waitingPeriod.detail: No divorce decree may be granted until at least 30 days after the complaint is filed.

grounds.detail: No-fault: spouses lived separate and apart for 18 continuous months without cohabitation. Fault grounds include adultery and cruelty.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital property is divided one-half to each spouse unless the court finds that inequitable and explains its reasons.

residency.detail: One spouse must live in California 6 months and in the filing county 3 months; legal separation has no minimum.

waitingPeriod.detail: A divorce is not final until 6 months after service of the summons and petition or the respondent's appearance.

grounds.detail: Irreconcilable differences that caused the irremediable breakdown of the marriage, or permanent legal incapacity to make decisions.

propertyDivision.detail: The community estate is divided equally.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The statewide formula CS = K[HN − (H%)(TN)] uses both parents' net incomes and parenting time.

legalSeparation.detail: Legal separation may be sought on the same grounds as divorce without meeting the residency rule.

residency.detail: One spouse must be domiciled in Colorado for 91 days before the case is filed.

waitingPeriod.detail: Decree can enter only after 91 days have passed since the court gained jurisdiction over the respondent (service or joining the petition).

grounds.detail: The marriage is irretrievably broken.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital property is divided in proportions the court deems just, without regard to marital misconduct.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The guideline uses the parents' combined gross income to set the basic obligation.

legalSeparation.detail: A decree of legal separation is entered on the same findings as dissolution.

residency.detail: 12 months' residence before filing or before the decree; exceptions if domiciled in CT at marriage and returned, or the cause arose after moving there.

waitingPeriod.detail: A contested trial cannot begin until 90 days after the return date; a joint nonadversarial petition can be decided no sooner than 30 days after filing.

grounds.detail: No-fault: the marriage has broken down irretrievably, or 18 months apart due to incompatibility. Fault grounds include adultery.

legalSeparation.detail: A decree of legal separation may be granted on the same causes as dissolution.

residency.detail: Either spouse must have lived in Delaware (or been stationed there) continuously for 6 or more months before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: No post-filing wait, but a no-fault divorce generally requires 6 months living separate and apart before the ruling.

grounds.detail: The marriage is irretrievably broken and reconciliation is improbable (shown by separation, misconduct, mental illness or incompatibility).

propertyDivision.detail: The court equitably divides marital property without regard to marital misconduct.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Delaware Family Court's child support formula is the Melson formula.

legalSeparation.detail: Delaware's Divorce and Annulment Act provides no legal separation action.

residency.detail: One spouse must be a bona fide D.C. resident for 6 months before filing; limited exception for same-sex marriages performed in D.C.

waitingPeriod.detail: No waiting or separation period; since a 2025 amendment, divorce may be granted when a spouse asserts they no longer wish to remain married.

grounds.detail: Divorce may be granted on one or both spouses' assertion that they no longer wish to remain married.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital property is distributed in an equitable, just and reasonable manner.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The basic obligation comes from a schedule using both parents' combined adjusted gross income, then is prorated by income.

legalSeparation.detail: Legal separation from bed and board may be granted when a spouse intends to pursue a separate life without divorce.

residency.detail: One spouse must reside in Florida for 6 months before filing the petition.

waitingPeriod.detail: No final judgment until 20 days after the petition is filed, unless the court finds injustice would result.

grounds.detail: The marriage is irretrievably broken, or one spouse has been adjudged mentally incapacitated for at least 3 years.

propertyDivision.detail: Courts start from an equal split of marital assets and debts unless factors justify an unequal division.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Both parents' net incomes are combined and applied to the guidelines schedule.

legalSeparation.detail: Florida has no legal separation, but a spouse may seek alimony and child support without divorce.

residency.detail: The filing spouse must be a bona fide Georgia resident for 6 months; a nonresident may sue a spouse who meets that rule.

waitingPeriod.detail: A no-fault divorce cannot be granted until at least 30 days after service on the respondent.

grounds.detail: No-fault: the marriage is irretrievably broken. Twelve fault grounds include adultery, desertion and cruel treatment.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Both parents' adjusted incomes are combined to find the basic obligation, which is split by each parent's share.

legalSeparation.detail: Separate maintenance is available when spouses live apart and no divorce is pending.

grounds.detail: The marriage is irretrievably broken, or the spouses have lived apart 2+ years (including under a separation or separate maintenance decree).

propertyDivision.detail: The court divides the estate as appears just and equitable.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Hawaii's Child Support Guidelines use the Melson formula.
childSupportGuidelines.cite: Haw. Rev. Stat. § 576D-7; Hawaii Child Support Guidelines

legalSeparation.detail: Separation from bed and board up to 2 years may be decreed when the marriage is temporarily disrupted.

residency.detail: The plaintiff must be an Idaho resident for 6 full weeks before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: No final decree until at least 21 days after the action is commenced and process is served.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irreconcilable differences. Fault grounds include adultery, extreme cruelty and desertion.

propertyDivision.detail: Community property is divided substantially equally unless there are compelling reasons otherwise.

residency.detail: One spouse must reside in Illinois (or be stationed there) for 90 days before filing or before findings.

waitingPeriod.detail: No mandatory wait; living apart 6 months before judgment creates an irrebuttable presumption that irreconcilable differences exist.

grounds.detail: Irreconcilable differences have caused the irretrievable breakdown of the marriage.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital property is divided in just proportions without regard to marital misconduct.

legalSeparation.detail: A spouse living apart may seek reasonable support and maintenance through legal separation.

residency.detail: 6 months in Indiana and 3 months in the filing county (or a military installation there) before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: The final hearing cannot be held earlier than 60 days after the petition is filed.

grounds.detail: Irretrievable breakdown is the no-fault ground; limited others include felony conviction, impotency and incurable insanity.

propertyDivision.detail: Courts presume an equal division of marital property is just and reasonable, subject to rebuttal.

legalSeparation.detail: Indiana establishes a cause of action for legal separation.

residency.detail: The petitioner must have been an Iowa resident for the last year, unless the respondent is an Iowa resident served personally.

waitingPeriod.detail: No decree until 90 days after original notice is served (or publication/waiver), unless waived for good cause.

grounds.detail: A breakdown of the marriage relationship so that the legitimate objects of matrimony are destroyed.

propertyDivision.detail: All property except inheritances and gifts is divided equitably after weighing statutory factors.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The schedule uses the parents' combined adjusted net incomes.

legalSeparation.detail: Separate maintenance actions proceed like dissolution actions.

residency.detail: The petitioner or respondent must have been an actual Kansas resident for 60 days before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: A divorce cannot be heard until 60 days after the petition is filed, unless an emergency is declared.

grounds.detail: Incompatibility is the no-fault ground; also failure to perform a material marital duty, or incompatibility from mental illness.

propertyDivision.detail: The court makes a just and reasonable division of property after weighing statutory factors.

legalSeparation.detail: A decree of separate maintenance may be granted on the same grounds as divorce.

residency.detail: One spouse must reside in Kentucky (or be stationed there) for 180 days before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: No decree until spouses have lived apart 60 days; with minor children, no testimony until 60 days after service.

grounds.detail: The marriage is irretrievably broken.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital property is divided in just proportions without regard to marital misconduct.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Support uses the parents' combined monthly adjusted parental gross income.

legalSeparation.detail: A decree of legal separation is granted on request unless the other party objects.

residency.detail: A spouse must be domiciled in Louisiana; 6 months' residence in a parish creates a rebuttable presumption of domicile.

waitingPeriod.detail: No-fault divorce requires living apart 180 days (no minor children) or 365 days (minor children).

grounds.detail: No-fault: living separate and apart for the required period. Fault: adultery, felony with hard labor, abuse, or a protective order.

propertyDivision.detail: Each spouse owns a present undivided one-half interest in community property.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The guideline uses both parties' combined adjusted gross income.

legalSeparation.detail: Separation from bed and board is available only in covenant marriages.

residency.detail: 6 months' residence, or no minimum if the plaintiff resides in Maine and the parties married or lived there when the cause arose.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irreconcilable marital differences. Fault grounds include adultery and cruel and abusive treatment.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital property is divided in proportions the court considers just after weighing statutory factors.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The parents' incomes are added for a combined annual gross income applied to the support table.

legalSeparation.detail: Maine provides for judicial separation.

residency.detail: Required only if the grounds arose outside Maryland; otherwise no minimum period applies.

waitingPeriod.detail: No post-filing wait; the 6-month separation ground requires 6 months apart before filing.

grounds.detail: Absolute divorce for 6-month separation, irreconcilable differences, or mutual consent with a signed settlement agreement.

propertyDivision.detail: The court may transfer interests or grant a monetary award to adjust the equities in marital property.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The schedule uses the parents' combined adjusted actual income.

legalSeparation.detail: Limited divorce was repealed effective Oct. 1, 2023; only absolute divorce remains.

residency.detail: 1 year if the grounds arose outside MA; no minimum if the plaintiff is domiciled in MA and the grounds arose there.

waitingPeriod.detail: Contested no-fault (1B): no hearing until 6 months after filing. Agreed no-fault (1A): judgment nisi after court approval.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irretrievable breakdown of the marriage. Fault grounds include adultery, desertion and cruel and abusive treatment.

propertyDivision.detail: The court may assign to either spouse all or part of the other's estate after weighing statutory factors.

legalSeparation.detail: A spouse with justifiable cause to live apart may seek separate support.

residency.detail: 180 days in Michigan and 10 days in the filing county, with limited exceptions to the county rule.

waitingPeriod.detail: No proofs until 60 days after filing, or 6 months if there are minor children (may be shortened for hardship).

grounds.detail: A breakdown of the marriage relationship so that the objects of matrimony are destroyed.

legalSeparation.detail: Separate maintenance may be filed on the same grounds as divorce.

residency.detail: One spouse must have resided (or been domiciled or stationed) in Minnesota for 180 days before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: No general waiting period; for a joint declaration (summary) dissolution, the decree is entered 30 days after filing.

grounds.detail: An irretrievable breakdown of the marriage relationship.

propertyDivision.detail: The court makes a just and equitable division of marital property without regard to misconduct.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The basic obligation is set from the parents' combined parental income.

legalSeparation.detail: A decree of legal separation is granted when one or both parties need it.

residency.detail: One spouse must be an actual bona fide Mississippi resident for 6 months before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: An irreconcilable-differences complaint must be on file 60 days before it can be heard.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irreconcilable differences (needs both spouses' consent). Twelve fault grounds include adultery and habitual cruel treatment.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Support is a percentage of the paying parent's adjusted gross income: 14% for one child up to 26% for five or more.

residency.detail: One spouse must be a Missouri resident (or stationed there) for 90 days before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: Judgment requires that 30 days have passed since the petition was filed.

grounds.detail: No reasonable likelihood the marriage can be preserved, so it is irretrievably broken; misconduct may be shown as evidence.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital property and debts are divided in proportions the court deems just after weighing statutory factors.

legalSeparation.detail: The court may enter a judgment of legal separation instead of dissolution.

residency.detail: One spouse must be domiciled in Montana (or stationed there) for 90 days before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: A decree may not be entered until 21 days after the date of service.

grounds.detail: Irretrievably broken, shown by 180+ days living apart or serious marital discord with no reasonable prospect of reconciliation.

propertyDivision.detail: The court equitably apportions all property, however and whenever acquired, without regard to misconduct.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Montana's guidelines (ARM 37.62) use the Melson formula.

legalSeparation.detail: A decree of legal separation may be entered on the same findings as dissolution.

residency.detail: 1 year's residence before filing, or married in Nebraska with one spouse residing there since the marriage.

waitingPeriod.detail: No divorce may be heard or tried until 60 days after service of process is perfected.

grounds.detail: The marriage is irretrievably broken.

propertyDivision.detail: Courts make an equitable division of the marital estate under the statute and case law.

legalSeparation.detail: Legal separation decrees adjust property, support and custody without dissolving the marriage.

residency.detail: A spouse must have resided in Nevada at least 6 weeks before filing, unless the cause arose in the county while both lived there.

waitingPeriod.detail: Nevada law sets no mandatory waiting period after filing.

grounds.detail: Incompatibility, living separate and apart 1 year, or insanity existing 2 years.

propertyDivision.detail: Courts make an equal disposition of community property unless there is a compelling reason for an unequal one.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Support is a tiered percentage of the obligor's gross monthly income under NAC chapter 425.

legalSeparation.detail: Nevada allows actions for separate maintenance.

residency.detail: 1 year if only the plaintiff is domiciled in NH; no minimum if both spouses are domiciled there, or the plaintiff is and the defendant is served in NH.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irreconcilable differences causing the irremediable breakdown of the marriage. Fault grounds include adultery and extreme cruelty.

propertyDivision.detail: Courts presume an equal division is equitable unless it would not be appropriate.

legalSeparation.detail: Legal separation may be decreed in any case where a divorce could be, but neither spouse may remarry.

residency.detail: One spouse must be a bona fide NJ resident for 1 year before filing, except when the ground is adultery.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irreconcilable differences for 6 months, or 18 months living apart. Fault grounds include adultery and extreme cruelty.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital property is distributed equitably using statutory criteria.

legalSeparation.detail: Divorce from bed and board (a form of legal separation) is available on the divorce grounds.

residency.detail: One spouse must have resided in New Mexico 6 months before filing and be domiciled there.

grounds.detail: No-fault: incompatibility. Fault grounds: cruel and inhuman treatment, adultery, or abandonment.

propertyDivision.detail: Property acquired by either spouse during marriage, other than separate property, is community property.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The basic obligation is based on both parents' combined income and paid proportionately.

legalSeparation.detail: Permanently separated spouses may seek property division, custody or alimony without a divorce.

residency.detail: 2 years' residence, or 1 year if married or lived in NY as spouses or the grounds arose there; none if grounds arose in NY and both live there.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irretrievable breakdown for at least 6 months, with economic issues resolved first. Fault grounds include adultery and cruel treatment.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital property is distributed equitably based on the circumstances of the case and the parties.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Child support percentages (17% for one child to 35%+ for five) apply to combined parental income, then are prorated.

legalSeparation.detail: A spouse may sue for a judgment of separation from bed and board.

residency.detail: One spouse must be a North Carolina resident for at least 6 months before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: Absolute divorce requires that the spouses have lived separate and apart for 1 year before filing.

grounds.detail: Absolute divorce for 1 year's separation or incurable insanity; fault matters only for divorce from bed and board.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital and divisible property is divided equally unless the court finds equal division is not equitable.

legalSeparation.detail: Divorce from bed and board is available for fault such as abandonment or cruel treatment.

residency.detail: The plaintiff must be a resident for 6 months before filing, or before the decree is entered.

waitingPeriod.detail: North Dakota law sets no mandatory waiting period after filing.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irreconcilable differences. Fault grounds include adultery, extreme cruelty and willful desertion.

propertyDivision.detail: The court makes an equitable distribution of the parties' property and debts.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Support is a varying percentage of the obligor's net income.

legalSeparation.detail: A temporary or permanent decree of separation may be granted for any cause allowing divorce.

residency.detail: The plaintiff must be an Ohio resident for at least 6 months before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: A divorce can't be heard until 42 days after service; for dissolution, the hearing is 30 to 90 days after filing.

grounds.detail: No-fault: incompatibility unless denied, or 1 year living apart. Fault grounds include adultery and extreme cruelty.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital property is divided equally unless that would be inequitable.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The basic schedule is based on the parents' combined annual income.

legalSeparation.detail: Either spouse may file a complaint for legal separation.

residency.detail: The plaintiff must be an actual Oklahoma resident in good faith for 6 months before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: With minor children, no final order until 90 days after filing, unless waived for good cause.

grounds.detail: No-fault: incompatibility. Fault grounds include abandonment for 1 year, adultery and extreme cruelty.

propertyDivision.detail: Jointly acquired property is divided as may appear just and reasonable.

residency.detail: 6 months' residence or domicile before filing if the marriage was not performed in Oregon; separation needs residence only at filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: Oregon law sets no mandatory waiting period after filing.

grounds.detail: Irreconcilable differences that have caused the irremediable breakdown of the marriage.

propertyDivision.detail: Property of either or both spouses is divided as may be just and proper in all the circumstances.

legalSeparation.detail: A suit for separation may be filed if one spouse is a resident when it is filed.

residency.detail: At least one spouse must be a bona fide Pennsylvania resident for 6 months before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: Mutual-consent divorce needs 90 days after filing; contested no-fault needs 1 year living separate and apart.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irretrievable breakdown by mutual consent or after 1 year apart. Fault grounds include adultery and desertion.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital property is divided equitably, without regard to misconduct, in percentages the court deems just.

residency.detail: The plaintiff (or a served defendant) must be domiciled in Rhode Island for 1 year before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: A divorce judgment becomes final 3 months after the trial and decision.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irreconcilable differences that caused the irremediable breakdown of the marriage; fault grounds also exist.

propertyDivision.detail: The court may assign either spouse a portion of the other's estate after weighing statutory factors.

legalSeparation.detail: Divorce from bed and board may be granted for any divorce cause or other appropriate causes.

residency.detail: 1 year if one spouse lives in South Carolina; 3 months if both spouses are residents.

waitingPeriod.detail: No final decree until 3 months after filing; the no-fault ground also requires 1 year living apart.

grounds.detail: No-fault: living separate and apart without cohabitation for 1 year. Fault: adultery, desertion, physical cruelty, habitual drunkenness.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital property is equitably apportioned using statutory factors.

legalSeparation.detail: Actions for separate maintenance and support are available.

residency.detail: The plaintiff must be a South Dakota resident (or stationed there) when filing; no minimum period or later residence required.

waitingPeriod.detail: No hearing or decree until 60 days after the summons and complaint are served.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irreconcilable differences. Fault grounds include adultery, extreme cruelty and willful desertion.

propertyDivision.detail: Courts make an equitable division of property belonging to either or both spouses.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The parents' combined monthly net incomes set the obligation, divided by each parent's share.

legalSeparation.detail: Separate maintenance may be sought without divorce on any divorce ground.

residency.detail: Required if the grounds arose outside Tennessee or the plaintiff then lived elsewhere; either spouse may meet it.

waitingPeriod.detail: Irreconcilable-differences cases must be on file 60 days (no minor children) or 90 days (minor children) before hearing.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irreconcilable differences, or 2+ years living apart with no minor children. Many fault grounds also exist.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital property is divided equitably, without regard to marital fault.

legalSeparation.detail: Tennessee law provides for legal separation.

residency.detail: Either spouse must be domiciled in Texas 6 months and live in the filing county 90 days before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: A divorce cannot be granted before the 60th day after filing, with exceptions for family violence.

grounds.detail: No-fault: the marriage has become insupportable because of discord or conflict. Fault grounds include cruelty and adultery.

propertyDivision.detail: The community estate is divided in a manner the court deems just and right.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Support is a percentage of the obligor's net resources (20% for one child, rising with more children).

waitingPeriod.detail: No divorce hearing until 30 days after the complaint is filed, unless extraordinary circumstances exist.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irreconcilable differences, or 3 years apart under separate maintenance. Fault grounds include adultery and desertion.

propertyDivision.detail: The divorce decree may include equitable orders relating to property and debts.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Parents pay proportionate shares of a base combined child support obligation.

legalSeparation.detail: Utah allows separate maintenance actions, including property and support orders.

residency.detail: 6 months' residence to file; one spouse must have lived in Vermont 1 year before the final hearing.

waitingPeriod.detail: The no-fault ground requires living apart 6 consecutive months; a decree also needs 1 year's residence.

grounds.detail: No-fault: living apart 6 consecutive months with resumption of marital relations not reasonably probable. Fault grounds also exist.

propertyDivision.detail: The court equitably divides and assigns all property, however and whenever acquired.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The guideline is based on the parents' combined available income.

legalSeparation.detail: Vermont provides for legal separation.

residency.detail: One spouse must be a bona fide Virginia resident and domiciliary for 6 months before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: No-fault divorce requires 1 year apart, or 6 months if there are no minor children and a separation agreement.

grounds.detail: No-fault: living separate and apart without cohabitation for the required period. Fault grounds include adultery, felony and cruelty.

propertyDivision.detail: The court classifies property and may grant a monetary award to achieve a fair and equitable result.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The basic obligation is computed from the parents' combined monthly gross income.

legalSeparation.detail: Divorce from bed and board is available on fault grounds.

residency.detail: The petitioner must be a Washington resident (or military member stationed there); no minimum period.

waitingPeriod.detail: The court acts only after 90 days have passed since both filing and service of the summons.

grounds.detail: The marriage is irretrievably broken.

propertyDivision.detail: The court disposes of community and separate property as appears just and equitable.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The economic table sets the basic obligation from the parents' combined monthly net income.

legalSeparation.detail: A legal separation may be entered instead of dissolution.

residency.detail: 1 year's residence; none if married in West Virginia and one spouse lives there at filing.

grounds.detail: No-fault: irreconcilable differences (admitted by answer), or 1 year living separate and apart. Fault grounds include adultery and cruelty.

propertyDivision.detail: Marital property is divided equally unless statutory factors justify a different division.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: The basic support table uses the parents' combined gross monthly income.

residency.detail: 6 months in Wisconsin and 30 days in the filing county before filing.

waitingPeriod.detail: No final hearing until 120 days after service (or filing of a joint petition), except emergencies.

grounds.detail: The marriage is irretrievably broken.

propertyDivision.detail: Wisconsin is a marital (community) property state; divisible property is presumed to be split equally.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Support is a percentage of the payer's income under the DCF 150 standard.

legalSeparation.detail: A judgment of legal separation may be granted.

residency.detail: 60 days before filing, or married in Wyoming with one spouse residing there since the marriage.

waitingPeriod.detail: A divorce decree cannot be entered less than 20 days after the complaint is filed.

grounds.detail: Irreconcilable differences in the marital relationship, or incurable insanity with confinement.

propertyDivision.detail: The court disposes of the parties' property as appears just and equitable.

childSupportGuidelines.detail: Presumptive tables use the parents' combined net income.

legalSeparation.detail: Judicial separation may be sought when grounds for divorce exist.
